title: Nicodemus, Mary, and the Sabbath: What The Chosen Gets Right Emotionally But Wrong Spiritually
paragraphs:
Nicodemus, Mary, and the Sabbath: What The Chosen Gets Right Emotionally But Wrong Spiritually
(The Chosen "The Sabbath" Season 1 Episode 2)

It’s the Sabbath.
The candles are lit.
Mary, once tormented by demons, is clean and calm.
She’s preparing food. Smiling. Peaceful.
Then the knock on the door comes…
Jesus enters. No dramatic entrance. No fiery message.
Just… a smile.

Everyone is stunned.
Jesus joins the dinner. The music swells. Emotions rise.
Millions of viewers tear up.
But what if this was emotionally powerful—and yet spiritually incomplete?

What if the Jesus who enters homes…
...never confronts sin
...never declares repentance
...never reveals Himself as Lord?

That’s not Jesus of Nazareth.
That’s Jesus of Netflix.

❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, isn’t it beautiful to show Jesus eating with sinners and joining their traditions? Doesn’t that show His humility?”
📖 MAIN BIBLE VERSE – Mark 1:14–15 (KJV):

“Now after that John was put in prison, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God,
And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand:
repent ye, and believe the gospel.”

🔥 The first words of the real Jesus weren’t emotional or poetic.
They were confrontational, authoritative, and eternally urgent.

🚨 THE TRUTH: What This Blog Will Reveal
✔️ The beautiful danger of sentimental storytelling about Jesus
✔️ Why The Chosen’s Shabbat scene is subtly misleading
✔️ How emotion replaces repentance in soft Christianity
✔️ What the real Jesus actually did when entering homes
✔️ Why Nicodemus’ portrayal lacks biblical follow-through

THE CORE TRUTH REVEALED – WHAT DOES THE BIBLE SAY?
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, didn’t Jesus sit with sinners and honor traditions like Sabbath meals? Isn’t that what The Chosen is showing?”
🔥 Let’s look at what Jesus actually did—not what feels good on screen.

📖 WHAT JESUS DID WHEN HE ENTERED HOMES:
Luke 19:5–10 (KJV) – Jesus and Zacchaeus

“Zacchaeus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house...
And Jesus said unto him, This day is salvation come to this house...
For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.”

💥 Jesus didn’t just sit and smile. He confronted the sinner.
✔ Zacchaeus immediately repented.
✔ Jesus declared salvation over him—not comfort.

📖 WHAT JESUS PREACHED—RIGHT FROM THE START:
Mark 1:15 (KJV)
“...Repent ye, and believe the gospel.”
Luke 5:32 (KJV)
“I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
🔥 Every time Jesus entered a scene—He brought a GOSPEL MISSION, not a cinematic moment.

⚠ WHAT THE CHOSEN SHOWED INSTEAD (EPISODE 2 – “SHABBAT”):
Mary prepares for Sabbath
Friends gather for a peaceful meal
Jesus shows up at the door, says nothing profound, and just joins quietly
Emotional music plays. That’s it.

🚨 NO CALL TO REPENTANCE.
🚨 NO DECLARATION OF HIS KINGSHIP.
🚨 NO TRUTH ABOUT WHO HE IS.
Just a gentle smile and subtle presence—dangerously vague and cinematic.

🔥 BIBLICAL JESUS VS. CINEMATIC JESUS (NO TABLE FORMAT)
The real Jesus:
Preached repentance openly
Declared Himself the Son of God
Divided crowds with truth
Called out hypocrisy and false religion
Healed with power and purpose
Never tiptoed around identity or authority
The Chosen’s Jesus (Episode 2):
Says almost nothing
Enters like a guest, not a King
Avoids truth confrontation
Supports tradition without Gospel correction
Inspires emotion without biblical clarity

📖 JESUS REBUKED EMPTY TRADITION:
Mark 7:6–9 (KJV):

“This people honoureth me with their lips, but their heart is far from me...
Laying aside the commandment of God, ye hold the tradition of men...
Full well ye reject the commandment of God, that ye may keep your own tradition.”
🔥 Jesus didn’t romanticize Shabbat—He rebuked those who honored it without heart-change.

💭 READER QUESTION:
“But isn’t it okay to show Jesus being gentle and relational first?”

✔ Jesus was gentle…
🔥 But never at the cost of truth.
🔥 Never at the cost of His identity.
🔥 Never at the cost of confronting sin.

BIBLICAL & HISTORICAL PROOF – CONFIRMING THE TRUTH
📖 JESUS NEVER JUST "JOINED THE TABLE" WITHOUT BRINGING TRUTH
Luke 7:36–50 (KJV) – Jesus at Simon the Pharisee’s house

A woman with a sinful past washes Jesus’ feet with her tears.
The Pharisee judges her.
Jesus speaks directly, rebukes the Pharisee, honors the woman’s faith, and declares:
“Thy sins are forgiven.”
🔥 Even in quiet meals, Jesus didn't blend in—He disrupted sin, exposed hearts, and exalted truth.

📖 JESUS DIDN’T GLORIFY TRADITION—HE EXPOSED ITS SHALLOWNESS
Matthew 12:1–8 (KJV) – Jesus is confronted about His disciples breaking Sabbath tradition.
🔥 His response?
“For the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day.” (v. 8)
💥 Jesus declared His lordship over Shabbat, not His gentle appreciation of it.

📖 NICODEMUS’ REAL ENCOUNTER – NOT JUST INTRIGUE, BUT TRUTH
John 3:1–7 (KJV):
“Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”

✔ In The Chosen, Nicodemus is shown as emotionally conflicted.
✔ In the Bible, Jesus confronts him with the hard truth—you must be born again.
📖 John 3:11 (KJV):
“We speak that we do know, and testify that we have seen; and ye receive not our witness.”
🔥 Jesus didn’t let Nicodemus drift in curiosity—He dropped spiritual fire on him.

🏺 HISTORICAL & PROPHETIC SUPPORT
📜 EARLY CHURCH WRITINGS – JESUS WAS NEVER “JUST A GUEST”
Justin Martyr (c. 150 AD) – Apology 1, Chapter 14:
Describes Jesus as “more than man... a divine power who rebuked, healed, cast out, and taught with divine authority.”
✔ There is no early church record of Jesus being portrayed as merely emotional, passive, or subtly mystical.

📖 PROPHETIC EXPECTATION – MESSIAH WOULD CONFRONT & COMMAND
Isaiah 42:6–7 (KJV):
“...to open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the prison...”

✔ That’s confrontation.
✔ That’s liberation with power—not dinner table subtlety.
📖 Isaiah 53:5 (KJV):
“He was wounded for our transgressions… the chastisement of our peace was upon him…”
🔥 The Messiah was sent to carry our sin, not sit comfortably in our traditions.

💥 THE DANGER OF A PASSIVE JESUS:
📖 2 Corinthians 11:4 (KJV):
“For if he that cometh preacheth another Jesus... ye might well bear with him.”

🧠 The longer people see Jesus portrayed as passive, subtle, and silent,
the more likely they are to accept the Antichrist who will come in peace, flattery, and charisma (Daniel 11:21).

💭 READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, why does it matter if they show Jesus soft in just one episode?”

🔥 Because that “one episode” becomes the lens through which people see all of Jesus.
And that is spiritual warfare through misrepresentation.
